votes.motion: Close the public hearing on the Sky Harbour Hangar Development TEFRA hearing.
votes.description: Closes the Tax Equity and Fiscal Responsibility Act public hearing regarding the Sky Harbour aircraft storage facility development at Salt Lake City International Airport, funded through a tax-exempt private activity bond with no financial liability to the City.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and adopt Ordinance 73 of 2025, approving Items E-2 Jordan River Restoration & Recreation Project Grant for $666,000 and Item E-3 FY26 Homeless Shelter Cities Mitigation Grant for $3,249,704 as proposed by the Administration, and deferring item E-1 COPS Technology & Equipment Grant – Subaward from Davis County for $224,000 to a future meeting.
votes.description: Adopts Budget Amendment No. 3 for FY2025-26 partially, approving grants for Jordan River restoration and homeless shelter mitigation while deferring the license plate reader camera grant pending further policy review on data privacy and use.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and adopt Resolution 42 of 2025, authorizing the release of Salt Lake City's reversionary interest in the property currently owned by Valley Behavioral Health at 107 South 800 West.
votes.description: Authorizes the release of the City's reversionary interest in property at 107 South 800 West to allow development of Saltair Lofts, a 68-unit permanent supportive housing project, in exchange for a 50-year Restrictive Use Agreement ensuring affordable permanent supportive housing for formerly homeless individuals.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinances 74A, 74B, 74C, and 74D of 2025 that include eliminating the 100-foot maximum building length and increasing the maximum number of dwelling units per building to 50 in the RMF-45 zoning district.
votes.description: Amends Title 21A of the Salt Lake City Code to update RMF-35 and RMF-45 multi-family zoning districts, removing barriers to housing development by introducing design standards, reducing minimum lot sizes, eliminating lot width minimums, permitting multiple buildings per lot, and offering a density bonus for preserving existing housing units.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 72 of 2025, enacting temporary zoning regulations authorizing temporary increase in overnight capacity at the youth homeless resource center at 888 South 400 West.
votes.description: Enacts a temporary zoning regulation allowing the Volunteers of America Youth Resource Center at 888 South 400 West to increase its maximum capacity up to fifty individuals, subject to building and fire code safety standards, for up to 180 days.

Approves setting a public hearing date for Consolidated Fee Schedule corrections for Public Utilities on January 13, 2026, and approves the appointment of Mark McGrath to the Historic Landmark Commission for a term ending December 9, 2029.
